chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who is in an obligatory prayer and stands up in the first two rak'ahs; is it permissible for him to grasp the side of the prayer niche (mihrab) to rise, relying on it for standing up without weakness or a specific ailment? He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.جَانِبَ الْمَسْجِدِ: The side of the prayer niche (mihrab)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use the mihrab for support when standing up during obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the permissibility of using the mihrab as a physical aid during the transition between rak'ahs, provided the act is not due to inherent weakness or illness. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between voluntary assistance and compensatory support for physical limitation, ensuring the prayer's validity remains intact without compromising its ritual purity.
